title: Tom Kha Gai: Coconut-Poached Chicken Breast with Galangal and Lime
changes_from_base: Instead of diced thighs simmered in a stock-and-coconut broth, whole chicken breasts are poached in an all-coconut-milk broth built on a pounded lemongrass, galangal, garlic and coriander-root paste, then sliced into the bowls.
summary: Whole chicken breasts gently poached in a rich coconut broth built on a pounded lemongrass and galangal paste, then sliced into bowls with mushrooms and lime.
equipment: pestle and mortar or mini food processor

ingredients.item: lemongrass stalk, tender core finely chopped
coriander stems (and roots, if you have them), chopped
lemongrass stalks, cut into 5 cm lengths and bruised

steps.title: Pound the paste
steps.text: Pound or blend the chopped lemongrass, galangal, garlic, coriander stems, shallots and peppercorns into a rough paste. Coarse is fine; bruising the fibres is what matters for flavour.

steps.title: Bloom in coconut
steps.text: Warm 100 ml of the coconut milk in the saucepan over medium heat until it bubbles. Stir in the paste and cook for 2 min until it smells fragrant. Frying the paste in coconut fat wakes up flavours that water alone would leave flat.

steps.title: Build the broth
steps.text: Add the remaining coconut milk, the water, lemongrass lengths and galangal slices. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 min.

steps.title: Poach the chicken
steps.text: Lower in the whole breasts, cover and hold the pot at the barest simmer for 14-16 min, turning them once, until the thickest part reads 74 °C. Rest them on the board for 5 min, then cut into 1 cm slices. Low, gentle heat is the secret to tender, moist breast meat.

steps.title: Cook the mushrooms
steps.text: Tip the mushrooms, lime leaves and chillies into the broth and simmer for 3 min.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Away from the heat, stir in the fish sauce and lime juice, then taste and adjust.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Arrange the sliced chicken in warm bowls, ladle the hot broth and mushrooms over and finish with coriander.

tips: The most common slip is letting the broth boil while the breasts poach; bubbles toughen the meat, so keep the surface barely moving.
Use a thermometer rather than cutting into the chicken to check it.
If the paste is too dry to blend, add a spoonful of the coconut milk.
storage: Keep the chicken and broth covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot (74 °C), without boiling hard. Not suitable for freezing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
